version.description: Protocol version, "major.minor": the oldest version that has every feature the document uses.

language.description: Language of the code, for highlighting and the language switcher, e.g. "pseudocode" or "python".

source.description: Source code of the algorithm in one language. When present, each step's `meta.line` must be a line of this code.

sources.description: The code in one or more languages, one entry per language, instead of `source`. Steps point into every language at once with `meta.at`.

language.description: Language of the code, for highlighting and the language switcher, e.g. "pseudocode" or "python".

propertyNames.description: Name of a point in the code, e.g. "swap" or "relax": lower-case kebab-case starting with a letter, at most 40 characters.

anchors.description: The 1-based line of each anchor in this code, e.g. { "swap": 6 }. Every anchor a step names must be here.

items.description: The code of the algorithm in one language, with its anchors.

propertyNames.description: Identifier of a structure, e.g. "arr" or "dist". Letters, digits and underscores; must not start with a digit; must not be a built-in JavaScript property name such as "constructor" or "__proto__".

place.description: Where the structure goes: "main" (default) with the main picture, or "side" for an auxiliary structure such as a queue, a call stack or a table of results. Side structures go right of the main ones in wide figures (slides, the player) and below them in narrow ones (notes).

view.description: How to draw the array: "row" (default); "tree", a complete binary tree where index i has children 2i+1 and 2i+2; or "heap", that tree with the row under it, both drawn from the one array, as textbooks draw heaps.

actions.description: Actions applied in order; a step may have none and only narrate.

id.description: Name of the kind of step, e.g. "compare", "relax" or "fixup-case-3": lower-case kebab-case starting with a letter, at most 40 characters. Names repeat; selectors such as "relax#3" refer to them.

at.description: With `sources`: the anchor of the code this step corresponds to, which every source maps to a line.

line.description: With `source`: the 1-based line this step corresponds to. With `sources`, use `at`.

narration.description: One or two sentences explaining the step to a learner.

items.description: One point on the timeline the learner can step to.

sections.description: Sections in order of their first step, e.g. one per operation. Steps before the first section belong to none.

id.description: Id of a section, unique within the document, e.g. "insert-5": lower-case kebab-case starting with a letter, at most 40 characters.

start.description: 0-based index of the section's first step. Each section starts after the one before.

items.description: A titled run of consecutive steps, such as one operation of a sequence. It lasts until the next section starts, or to the end of the document.

description: A step-by-step visualization: declared structures plus a timeline of steps, each applying actions to those structures.
